newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea accuses S.Korea of military provocation.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea accuses S.Korea of military provocation.

text.p: North Korea bitterly accused South Korea on Friday of launching military provocation near their heavily fortified border in order to intimidate it.
"(South Korea) successively conducted military manoeuvres and provocative acts that excessively irritated and intimidated our side (North Korea)," state-run Radio Pyongyang said.
In a broadcast monitored by the Tokyo-based Radiopress news agency, the radio said the South Korean military conducted massive military exercises near the border dividing the two Koreas on Wednesday.
Friday's condemnation of Seoul followed Pyongyang's repeated warnings that its armed forces were ready for a "final battle" against the Unites States and its ally South Korea.

In a rare statement on Wednesday last week, a North Korean military spokesman said recent South Korean amphibious exercises on islands near the North, as well as other U.S. exercises, showed that Seoul and Washington were set to strike while famine-stricken North was weak.
Severe floods destroyed food stocks and grain harvests in North Korea in 1995 and 1996, pushing the communist state to the brink of famine.

The U.S. State Department said on Wednesday that senior officials from the United States, North Korea and South Korea would meet in New York on Monday in a fresh step towards negotiating a formal end to the 1950-53 Korean War.

President Bill Clinton and South Korea's President Kim Young-sam proposed four-way peace talks in April last year between the two Koreas, the United States and China. The aim is to create a lasting peace to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War but left the two Koreas technically at war.
Famine-threatened North Korea in April agreed in principle to join the peace talks but tied participation to large-scale food aid and an easing of U.S. trade sanctions.
